The author is not responsible for any damage to your device, Glyph LEDs, or any other hardware. This project is distributed under the WTFPL license. > > *Manual commands (especially `led` and `progress`) are provided for testing and may behave unpredictably.* ## ✨ Features - **Start / Stop:** Manual control to turn all Glyphs on or off instantly. - **Brightness Control:** Smooth brightness adjustment (0–255) via WebUI or CLI. - **Wave Animation:** A software-based running wave effect. - **WebUI:** Convenient and clean control directly from your root manager. - **CLI (Termux):** Direct access via the `glyphctl` binary, including experimental `led` and `progress` commands. ## 📋 Requirements - **Device:** Nothing Phone (2a) *(tested on Android 17 / Nothing OS 5.0)*. - **Root Manager:** **KernelSU** (or a fork like ReSukiSU / SukiSU) or **Magisk**. - **Important for KernelSU users:** The `meta-overlayfs` metamodule is required for files in `system/bin` to be mounted correctly. > **ℹ️ Note on other devices:** Paths to the sysfs nodes may differ on Phone (1) or Phone (2). Check `/sys/devices/platform/soc/*.i2c/i2c-*/...` before installing. ## 📦 Installation 1. Download the latest `.zip` from the [**Releases**](../../releases) page. 2. Install the ZIP via your root manager (KernelSU, ReSukiSU, or Magisk). 3. **Reboot** your device. ## 🕹️ Usage ### 🌐 WebUI Open the module in your root manager and launch the WebUI. From there, you can control the brightness, start/stop the Glyphs, and trigger the wave animation. ### 💻 CLI (Termux) After installation, the utility is available at `/system/bin/glyphctl`: | Command | Description | | :--- | :--- | | `su -c 'glyphctl start'` | Turn all Glyphs on (manual mode, brightness 255) | | `su -c 'glyphctl stop'` | Turn all Glyphs off | | `su -c 'glyphctl brightness 128'` | Set brightness (0-255) | | `su -c 'glyphctl wave'` | Run the wave animation | | `su -c 'glyphctl led 5 255'` | 🧪 Experimental: control a single LED (ID 0-25) | | `su -c 'glyphctl progress 50'` | 🧪 Experimental: fill a percentage of the top strip (0-100) | ## ⚙️ How it works The module consists of two core parts: 1. **`glyphctl`**: A C utility that writes directly to the `aw20036` driver sysfs nodes (`/sys/devices/platform/soc/11e80000.i2c/i2c-3/3-003a/leds/aw20036_led/`). 2. **Daemon**: A background process (started via `service.sh`) that holds `operating_mode` at `1` (manual mode), preventing the Nothing system service from resetting it. It also listens to a FIFO (`/data/local/tmp/glyph_fifo`) for commands from external apps. ## 🐛 Known Issues - Individual LED mapping (IDs 0–25) may require further research. The `progress` command currently only affects the top 24 LEDs. - Aggressive system services may still cause brief conflicts; the daemon tries to recover the mode as quickly as possible. ## 🤝 Credits - The **Nothing community** for reverse-engineering the `aw20036` driver and sharing sysfs paths. - The **KernelSU** and **Magisk** developers for their module APIs and documentation. - **XDA Developers** forum for ongoing discussions and testing. ## 📄 License This project is licensed under the **WTFPL** (Do What The Fuck You Want To Public License). readmeHTML:
🌒 Glyph Keeper

Reclaiming Glyph control on Nothing Phone (2a).

![Platform](https://github.com/vaccrate/GlyphKeeper)

![Root Manager](#requirements)

![License](LICENSE)

![Status](#disclaimer)

---

After the update to Android 17 (Nothing OS 5.0), the system service responsible for Glyph management started aggressively resetting the LED driver's operating mode. This breaks third-party apps, automation, and any manual control over the Glyphs.

Glyph Keeper is a root module (KernelSU / Magisk) that bypasses the Nothing system service and communicates directly with the aw20036 LED driver via sysfs.

📑 Table of Contents

  • [⚠️ Disclaimer](#️-disclaimer)
  • [✨ Features](#-features)
  • [📋 Requirements](#-requirements)
  • [📦 Installation](#-installation)
  • [🕹️ Usage](#️-usage)
  • [⚙️ How it works](#️-how-it-works)
  • [🐛 Known Issues](#-known-issues)
  • [🤝 Credits](#-credits)
  • [📄 License](#-license)

    • ⚠️ Disclaimer

    > 🚨 EXPERIMENTAL MODULE

    > Use at your own risk. The author is not responsible for any damage to your device, Glyph LEDs, or any other hardware. This project is distributed under the WTFPL license.

    >

    > *Manual commands (especially led and progress) are provided for testing and may behave unpredictably.*

    ✨ Features

  • **Start / Stop:** Manual control to turn all Glyphs on or off instantly.
  • **Brightness Control:** Smooth brightness adjustment (0–255) via WebUI or CLI.
  • **Wave Animation:** A software-based running wave effect.
  • **WebUI:** Convenient and clean control directly from your root manager.
  • **CLI (Termux):** Direct access via the `glyphctl` binary, including experimental `led` and `progress` commands.

    • 📋 Requirements

  • **Device:** Nothing Phone (2a) *(tested on Android 17 / Nothing OS 5.0)*.
  • **Root Manager:** **KernelSU** (or a fork like ReSukiSU / SukiSU) or **Magisk**.
  • **Important for KernelSU users:** The `meta-overlayfs` metamodule is required for files in `system/bin` to be mounted correctly.

    • > ℹ️ Note on other devices: Paths to the sysfs nodes may differ on Phone (1) or Phone (2). Check /sys/devices/platform/soc/*.i2c/i2c-*/... before installing.

    📦 Installation

  • Download the latest `.zip` from the [**Releases**](../../releases) page.
  • Install the ZIP via your root manager (KernelSU, ReSukiSU, or Magisk).
  • **Reboot** your device.

    • 🕹️ Usage

    🌐 WebUI

    Open the module in your root manager and launch the WebUI. From there, you can control the brightness, start/stop the Glyphs, and trigger the wave animation.

    💻 CLI (Termux)

    After installation, the utility is available at /system/bin/glyphctl:

    | Command | Description |

    | :--- | :--- |

    | su -c 'glyphctl start' | Turn all Glyphs on (manual mode, brightness 255) |

    | su -c 'glyphctl stop' | Turn all Glyphs off |

    | su -c 'glyphctl brightness 128' | Set brightness (0-255) |

    | su -c 'glyphctl wave' | Run the wave animation |

    | su -c 'glyphctl led 5 255' | 🧪 Experimental: control a single LED (ID 0-25) |

    | su -c 'glyphctl progress 50' | 🧪 Experimental: fill a percentage of the top strip (0-100) |

    ⚙️ How it works

    The module consists of two core parts:

  • **`glyphctl`**: A C utility that writes directly to the `aw20036` driver sysfs nodes (`/sys/devices/platform/soc/11e80000.i2c/i2c-3/3-003a/leds/aw20036_led/`).
  • **Daemon**: A background process (started via `service.sh`) that holds `operating_mode` at `1` (manual mode), preventing the Nothing system service from resetting it. It also listens to a FIFO (`/data/local/tmp/glyph_fifo`) for commands from external apps.

    • 🐛 Known Issues

  • Individual LED mapping (IDs 0–25) may require further research. The `progress` command currently only affects the top 24 LEDs.
  • Aggressive system services may still cause brief conflicts; the daemon tries to recover the mode as quickly as possible.

    • 🤝 Credits

  • The **Nothing community** for reverse-engineering the `aw20036` driver and sharing sysfs paths.
  • The **KernelSU** and **Magisk** developers for their module APIs and documentation.
  • **XDA Developers** forum for ongoing discussions and testing.

    • 📄 License

    This project is licensed under the WTFPL (Do What The Fuck You Want To Public License). See the LICENSE file for details.
